title: Marco Polo on the Silk Road
description: 1271-1275. Escort the young Marco Polo, his father Niccolo, and their trade caravan across the deserts and mountain passes of Central Asia to the court of Kublai Khan. Bandit raiders and harsh terrain threaten the route; the caravan's pack animals must survive. Victory requires bringing Marco alive to the Khan's summer palace at Shangdu.

anachronisms_found: EL_CID as a member of the Polo caravan: Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar died in 1099, some 170 years before the journey, and was Castilian, not Venetian
FREDERICK_BARBAROSSA in the caravan: the Hohenstaufen emperor drowned in 1190 and never travelled the Silk Road; presumably stands in for Niccolo Polo, who is named in the text but never placed

Knights and Crossbowmen as caravan escort: the Polos travelled as a tiny merchant party with local guides and Mongol paiza-holders, not a Latin heavy-cavalry retinue; Trade Carts, camels or light foot would have been available in the engine
SHEEP used as the caravan's 'pack animals' when camels (Camel Rider / domesticated camel objects) and Trade Carts exist in the catalogue and are the iconic Silk Road transport

Shangdu represented by a plain European TOWN_CENTER plus two Gaia yurts; the Khan's summer palace could have been suggested with East Asian-style buildings, a Wonder, or Mongol/Chinese architecture set pieces
Kublai Khan himself is entirely absent from the objects despite the victory text describing Marco standing before him

issues_found: Marco Polo is represented by the EL_CID hero unit — a Castilian warlord who died in 1099, nearly two centuries before the journey; a renamed generic unit (or the Mongol/Persian civilian-style hero) would have avoided placing a different named historical figure on the map.
Niccolo Polo is represented by FREDERICK_BARBAROSSA, the 12th-century Holy Roman Emperor — again a wrong named figure where a renamed generic unit was available.
Kublai Khan, the destination and the second principal of the story, is never placed; Shangdu is only a Gaia TOWN_CENTER plus two yurts and flags, with no Khan figure or court at all.

Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the Venetian party and the Central Asian bandits may render in any architecture set — Teutonic, Japanese, Mesoamerican — undoing the yurt/tent dressing.

The Polo escort is built as a feudal European war band (2 KNIGHT, 2 CROSSBOWMAN, 2 SPEARMAN); the historical party was a tiny merchant family group travelling with guides, not a mounted lance detachment.
Trade goods and pack animals are modelled as SHEEP when the engine ships TRADE_CART (and camels), which would represent a Silk Road caravan far more legibly — an avoidable choice.

The two bandit ambushes are generic invented set-pieces; the specific hazards the Polos recorded (the Karaunas raiders of Persia, the Gobi crossing, Niccolo's brother Maffeo's presence in the party) are absent, and Maffeo Polo is simply omitted.

Marco Polo is represented by the EL_CID hero — an 11th-century Castilian warlord — and Niccolo Polo by FREDERICK_BARBAROSSA, a 12th-century Holy Roman Emperor. Both are figures of unrelated culture and century; the engine ships no Marco Polo hero, but a renamed generic unit (villager, trade cart escort, or even a monk) was available and would have been correct.

Kublai Khan, the destination and the man the whole journey is about, is not represented by any unit at all — the Khan's court at Shangdu is a single GAIA TOWN_CENTER with two flags, and no ruler figure or Mongol court retinue stands there.

Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the architecture of Player 1's Venetian caravan and Player 2's Central Asian raiders is left to chance rather than assigned (Italians/Mongols or Tatars/Cumans were all available).

The caravan's pack animals are SHEEP. The engine offers trade carts and camel units, which would represent Silk Road pack animals and trade goods far more faithfully; the narration even speaks of 'trade goods' that are nowhere placed.

The escort force is KNIGHT, CROSSBOWMAN and SPEARMAN — a Western European field detachment. The historical Polos travelled as a tiny merchant party of three with local guides, not with heavy cavalry and crossbowmen.
TREE_PALM_FOREST used throughout, including in the stretch narrated as the Pamir foothills, where palms are geographically impossible.
The raiders occupy ARCHERY_RANGE buildings and a dozen yurts, giving the 'bandits' a fixed settlement and military infrastructure they would not have had as caravan robbers.
